sections.html:
Caddo Parish is in the northwest corner of Louisiana, with Shreveport as its parish seat and largest city. The 2020 population was 237,848 across 937 square miles. Bossier Parish lies directly east, across the Red River. Besides Shreveport, the parish has the towns of Blanchard, Greenwood, Mooringsport, Oil City and Vivian and the villages of Belcher, Gilliam, Hosston, Ida and Rodessa, which gives owners several local governments to deal with.

Median household income was $42,003 in the 2020 American Community Survey. An owner on a tight income can fall behind on a bill that arrives once a year, and the parish runs an annual tax lien auction for unpaid balances.

sections.h2: Who handles Caddo Parish property tax?
sections.html:
The Caddo Parish Assessor values every parcel and the Caddo Parish Sheriff collects the parish tax. The Sheriff does not decide how much you owe, and the Assessor's Office is separate from the Sheriff.

  • Assessor: Caddo Parish Courthouse, Room 102, (318) 226-6701 for address changes and value questions.
  • Sheriff's Tax Department: Caddo Parish Courthouse, 1st Floor, 501 Texas Street, Room 101, Shreveport, open Monday to Friday from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM; phone (318) 681-0638 for balances.
  • Mail payments to the Property Tax Dept., P.O. Box 20905, Shreveport, LA 71120-0905.
  • Shreveport city tax is collected separately by the city, at (318) 673-5500, and does not appear on the Sheriff's notice.

Outside Shreveport, nine parish fire districts provide fire protection, and their fees are set by voters in each district. Shreveport residents fund fire service through city taxes instead.

sections.h2: How the Caddo assessor sets a value
sections.html:
Caddo uses three approaches: comparing recent sales, estimating replacement cost less depreciation, and looking at the income a property could earn. A sale made under pressure, such as an owner who needed cash fast, can distort a comparison, so the office studies many sales.

Louisiana then applies a fixed percentage to the market value to reach the assessed value.

  • Land: 10%.
  • Residential improvements, including apartments: 10%.
  • Commercial improvements: 15%.
  • Business movable property: 15%.
  • Public service, excluding land: 25%.

Millage then converts the assessed value to tax. Read your own notice for the rate that applies to your parcel.

An owner who lives in the home qualifies for the homestead exemption, which removes parish tax on the first $75,000 of market value. It applies to one home, not to city taxes, and not to fire district fees. File as soon as you become the owner; the exemption stays until the owner changes or the home stops being the primary residence.

  • Disabled veteran owners: a 100% service-connected rating, confirmed by a VA form, can qualify for up to $75,000 of additional homestead.
  • Age 65 and older: a special assessment level freezes the assessed value if adjusted gross income was under $100,000. It is lost if the property is transferred or improvements exceed 25% of its value, and a surviving spouse over 55 can qualify.
  • Disabled owners under 65: a freeze is available with 100% Social Security disability or a 50% service-connected rating, but it must be reapplied for each year.

The office requires proof of the previous year's income, such as a tax return or a Social Security statement.

Each year the Caddo assessor opens the books in mid August and closes public inspection at the end of that month. Appeals must be received by 5:00 p.m. on a deadline in early September, and the Board of Review hears them a few days later at the Caddo Commission. Call the office for the current dates.

Timing matters because the open-roll period is when an owner can legally file a protest. Many taxpayers wait for the bill that arrives around the first of December, and the office will discuss the assessment then, but a protest can no longer be filed at that point. Mark the late-August dates in your calendar.

sections.h2: When Caddo Parish property tax is due and what happens when it is late
sections.html:
Caddo taxes must be paid by December 31, and notices are generally mailed in the last week of November. After December 31 the tax is delinquent, with interest of 1% per month. Taxes not fully paid by January 31 add a 10% collection fee, and unpaid accounts after that date add the cost of notices and newspaper advertising.

Caddo Parish Sheriff payment rules
Charge or ruleDetail
Due dateDecember 31
Interest after December 311% per month
Collection fee10% if not fully paid by January 31
Personal or business checksAccepted only until the close of business on the last day of February
Mortgage companiesAsked to pay by December 20; postmarks of December 31 are accepted

Payments post to the account number you give, and a payment to the wrong account is final. Partial payments are allowed, but the unpaid balance keeps growing and the parcel is still offered at the annual auction.

sections.h2: What happens at a tax lien auction
sections.html:
The Sheriff sells a tax lien certificate at an online auction, held in the summer, and the winning bidder is the person who will take the least ownership interest in the property while paying the full unpaid taxes. That matches the new statewide lien approach that took effect January 1, 2026. A property that draws no bid is transferred to the parish, which can sometimes sell it to a third party.

Adjudicated property can be found through the CPTA Professional Search subscription or by visiting the courthouse; phone requests are not answered. Because the rules changed in 2026, a Caddo owner with a delinquent balance should ask the Sheriff what the lien process allows today.

sections.h2: How Caddo property tax works when you sell
sections.html:
The Sheriff does not split the bill between buyer and seller, so the full year's tax stays on the property until someone pays it. A buyer who closes after January 1 may find the account still in the prior owner's name, and the new owner is responsible for checking what is owed.

  • Get the current balance from the Sheriff's Tax Department before choosing a closing date.
  • Check city tax with Shreveport separately, since it is billed apart from the parish.
  • Ask your mortgage servicer for proof of payment if escrow covers the tax, because the Sheriff posts the first payment it receives and will not reverse a duplicate.
  • Have the new owner file for homestead soon after closing.

A house with taxes behind can still be sold if the title company pays the balance from proceeds. A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can close that way without waiting on a lender.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Caddo Parish?
faqs.a: The Caddo Parish Sheriff's Tax Department collects parish property tax at 501 Texas Street, Room 101, in Shreveport, or by mail to P.O. Box 20905. The Assessor sets the value but does not take payment.

faqs.q: Is Shreveport city tax on my Caddo Parish tax notice?
faqs.a: No. The Sheriff's notice covers parish taxes only. The City of Shreveport collects its own tax and can be reached at (318) 673-5500.

faqs.q: When do Caddo assessment appeals close?
faqs.a: Appeals must reach the assessor by 5:00 p.m. on a deadline in early September, after the books open in mid August. Call the office at (318) 226-6701 for the current date.

faqs.q: What are the penalties for paying Caddo tax late?
faqs.a: Interest runs at 1% per month after December 31. A 10% collection fee applies if the tax is not fully paid by January 31, and notice and advertising costs can follow.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Caddo Parish house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company can pay the delinquent tax, interest and fees from the sale proceeds. Get the payoff amount from the Sheriff's Tax Department first.
